title: Ties of a sort and the input order of aggregates are not guaranteed
verdict: `tie_order`: any order (`ORDER BY` may not be stable)
description: "ORDER BY may not use a stable algorithm": rows that tie on every key come out in any order. `JOIN`, `UNION`, `GROUP BY` and whole-table aggregation do not preserve the order of rows either; `FROM` a single table, `WHERE`, `SELECT`, `LIMIT`, `OFFSET`, `UNION ALL` and a window with an empty `OVER` do (Order Preservation).

`list` (`array_agg`) and `string_agg` are order-sensitive and "can have non-deterministic results without ordering"; an `ORDER BY` in the call sorts the values first, and the docs give that sort no stability either, so ties on its keys take any order.
For windows (`row_number`, `ntile`, `lag`, …) the docs only say that without an `ORDER BY` the results "are not well-defined"; the order of peers is for round 2.

Round 2 (source): every sort, `ORDER BY`, a window's partition and order, and an aggregate's `ORDER BY`, goes through the same `Sort`. Each thread sorts its rows' keys with vergesort, which falls back to ska_sort, an in-place radix sort; neither is stable, and the key holds only the sort columns. The threads' sorted runs are then merged (K-way Merge Path). Rows that tie on every key come out in an order that depends on the sort and on how rows were split between threads.

Windows: `row_number` is the row's position in its sorted partition, and `ntile` is computed from that position, so both depend on the order of peers. `rank`, `dense_rank`, `percent_rank` and `cume_dist` step at the start of each peer group and give every peer the same value, so they do not. `lag`, `lead`, `first_value`, `last_value` and `nth_value` read rows by their position in the frame, so a peer's value depends on the order of the peers.
reference: `tie_order`: any order of the ties (docs/core-semantics.md); the reference fixes nothing, and a plan that needs one order is refused or made `tie_free`. DuckDB's is one of them.
